# nooma

> Local semantic search over your files: find a document by what it is about, fully offline.

nooma keeps two indexes over the folders it is pointed at - full text for
exact words, vectors for meaning - and answers with one list from both. It is
a command-line program, `nooma`, and a window, over one library crate. Nothing
of what it reads leaves the machine. Everything below is written for people
and agents alike: there is no second set of instructions kept elsewhere.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what it is, what working with it looks like, how to install it
- [Getting Started](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started.md): install, search your folders, index a repository
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): the layout, the gate, how fixtures are made, how a release goes out
- [Architecture decisions](docs/adr/): why it is built the way it is, one decision per file
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): what each release changed

## Reference

- [find, similar, index, source](docs/src/content/docs/reference/find.md): searching folders, every option and the JSON each command prints
- [model](docs/src/content/docs/reference/model.md): fetching the embedding model
- [eval](docs/src/content/docs/reference/eval.md): measuring search against questions whose answers are known
- [repo](docs/src/content/docs/reference/repo.md): the repository index - symbols, imports, summaries, history by word, path and meaning
- [provider](docs/src/content/docs/reference/provider.md): the `FullText` trait of `nooma-core` - one folder searched by words and by meaning, for another program
